speaker: gm
text:
Prout turns slowly on the sack hoist above the shut loft door. A pigeon occupies the beam above him, with the calm of an official who has already filed its opinion. Below, a scrawny boy in enormous black boots lobs gutter stones at the body.

“Missed. Cob never misses. The dead’s just dodging.”

From the wall top, a sharp-faced girl in a shawl swears at him and the yard in two languages, neither of them complimentary.

Sergeant Kell steps away from the open gate, notebook in hand. “Sergeant Agnes Kell, investigator. The Captain calls it suicide.” Her pencil rests against the page; her face offers no verdict of its own.

A stone clangs off the hoist hook.

speech.tag: the boy in the too-big boots
speech.speaker: cob

speaker: player
text: (I stomp over and pluck the stone out of the boy's hand before he can throw it) OI. No stones at the dead. He can't dodge, and it's rude.

speaker: gm
text:
You cross the cobbles and pluck the stone from Cob’s fist. He jerks back, his other hand tightening around the stones he still has. The big boots creak as he plants his feet.

“OI! Cob was aiming at the hook. The dead don’t mind.” He glares up at you. “And Cob don’t talk to bluebottles.”

On the wall, the girl’s heels stop drumming. “Listen to her, Cob. She’s got the stone.”

Kell watches your hands, then makes a brief note. “Stone taken from the boy. No injury.”

marks.note: You took the stone from Cob, and he’s calling you a bluebottle—a name for the watch. He won’t talk to someone he sees as watch.

speaker: player
text: Not a bluebottle. I'm Grunda. King sent me. (I point at his boots) Those are big boots for a little boy. Where'd you get them?

speaker: gm
text:
Cob glances at the stones in your fist, then up at your face. His chin comes up a fraction.

“Cob found ’em.” He scuffs one oversized toe against the cobbles. “They’re Cob’s da’s. He’s got big feet.”

From the wall, the girl in the shawl snorts. “Your da’s boots? You’d need a second da to fill ’em.”

Cob’s ears redden. He stamps once; the left boot gives a small, dry crackle.

Kell’s pencil pauses above her notebook. “Grunda Ironjaw. The King’s investigator.” She makes a neat entry. “Name given. Boots disputed.”

speaker: player
text: That boot crackled. Boots don't crackle. (I crouch down to his level, big hand out, palm up) Something in there, little man. Show Grunda. I won't take it from you.

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to get Cob to let you look in his boot: 8 + 0 = 8 vs DC 12: failure

speaker: gm
text:
Cob snatches his foot back and clamps both hands over the boot.

“No! Cob said they’re Cob’s. You said you wouldn’t take ’em, and now you want to poke about in ’em.” His voice jumps sharp; the big boot scrapes over the cobbles as he backs toward the water butt.

The girl drops from the wall and plants herself between you and Cob, jaw set. “You heard him. Hands off his boots.”

Kell’s pencil moves. “Request to inspect the boy’s boot. Refused.”

speaker: player
text: Fine. Keep your boots. (I turn to the hanging man) Sergeant. We cut him down. Nobody should hang there for pigeons. (I grab the hoist rope and haul, taking his weight so he comes down gentle)

speaker: gm
text:
The hoist rope bites into your hands and barely shifts. It runs over the high beam, then through the slot above the loft door; the fastening is somewhere inside. Prout remains hanging above the cobbles.

Kell steps nearer, her gaze following the rope. “The rope’s fastened up there, investigator. We’ll need the ladder or access to the loft.”

The boy watches you from beneath his oversized boots, stones still clenched in his fist. The girl in the shawl says nothing.

speaker: player
text: Then we go up. (I look for the way into the granary loft — a door, stairs, a ladder) Where's the ladder? Who's got the key to this place?

speaker: gm
text:
You scan the yard for a ladder or a way through the granary doors. There’s no ladder in the swept-bare yard; the big doors are padlocked, and the loft door is barred from the inside.

Kell follows your glance to the doors. “The porters’ ladders are locked inside. The warden keeps the key; she’s at the palace. Her runner came back with ‘After the Assembly.’”

The girl in the shawl keeps her place beside Cob, watching you. Cob’s eyes flick toward the full water butt in the corner, then away.

“There is the body, investigator. I can hold a ladder if one appears.”

marks.note: During the Assembly, the city puts official business aside; people get told to wait until it’s over.

speaker: player
text: Don't need a ladder. (I go to the full water butt, wrap my arms round it, and heave it across the cobbles toward the spot under the body, to stand on)

speaker: dice
text: Athletics check to move the full water butt beneath the hanging man: 11 + 5 = 16 vs DC 16: success

speaker: gm
text:
You brace against the full butt and drag it across the cobbles. Water sloshes over the rim; the barrel grinds into place directly beneath Prout.

Kell grips its side as you climb up. The body swings within reach, the rope taut above him. From here you can see the noose’s dark, slanting mark at his throat—and, lower down, a thinner line running level around his neck.

Kell looks up at you, pencil ready. “I’ll steady the butt. Tell me what you see, investigator.”

speaker: player
text: Two marks. Rope mark goes up slanty. Other one goes flat, straight round. (I growl) Seen that in the army. Somebody choked him from behind first, then strung him up. This is no suicide, Sergeant. Write it big.

speaker: gm
text:
Kell looks from the two marks to your face. Her pencil moves across the notebook.

“You saw two marks: a slanting mark at the throat, and a level line around it. Your army experience tells you the level line was made before he was hoisted. Cause: strangulation. Manner: murder, made to look like suicide. Noted.”

The girl in the shawl has gone still. Cob’s stones lower in his hands.

Kell’s pencil pauses. “I’ll sign him in as a murder. I won’t write a name without evidence.” She glances toward the boy’s oversized boots. “The dead-cart comes at noon.”

speaker: player
text: (Still up on the butt, I look down at his feet, then pat down his coat and pockets) What's he got on him? Shoes, purse, papers?

speaker: gm
text:
Your hand finds only cold cloth and the slack weight of Prout’s coat. His pockets are empty of purse and papers; his feet are stockinged, his boots gone.

Kell keeps the water butt steady beneath you. “The porters found his satchel open and empty. His spectacles are by the gate. I’ve recorded both.”

Cob shifts back, eyes fixed on you from beneath the brim of the enormous boots. The girl in the shawl’s shoulders tighten. “You’ve had your look. Leave him be.”

speaker: player
text: (I climb down off the butt and sit on it, so I'm not looming) Cob. Those are his boots. Not your da's. I don't care that you took them, dead man don't need boots. But whatever crackles in there might catch who killed him. You want to help catch a strangler, or not?

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to get Cob to help catch the strangler: 1 + 0 = 1 vs DC 15: failure (natural 1!)

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s chin lifts. He clamps both hands over the left boot and backs toward the water butt.

“Cob don’t know nothing, and you’re not having them.”

The girl in the shawl shifts in front of him, eyes fixed on you.

“He’s answered, investigator.” Her pencil makes a short mark in the notebook. “You have your evidence of murder. Not his help.”

Cob edges toward the gap behind the butt. The left boot creaks softly as he moves.
